Market watchlist

Where should you look in 2026?

Start with market archetypes, not viral rankings. The strongest fit depends on your guest, capital, operating model and tolerance for regulation and seasonality.

Market rules, taxes and economics change. Every property requires current, address-specific verification before an offer.
01Drive-to

Gatlinburg, Tennessee

Study it for: year-round leisure, a proven cabin product and multiple regional attractions.

Micro-location: view quality, mountain-road access, park drive time and guest-friendly parking.

Main riskPrice + saturation
Best-fit operatorAmenity-led
02Leisure

Scottsdale, Arizona

Study it for: winter sun, events, golf, groups and premium outdoor living.

Rule snapshot: Scottsdale says rentals under 30 days need an annual city license; state TPT, neighbor notice and liability coverage also apply.

Main riskSeasonality + rules
Best-fit operatorCompliance-first
Verify with City of Scottsdale ↗
03Drive-to

Broken Bow, Oklahoma

Study it for: regional drive-to demand and a design-forward cabin category.

Micro-location: utilities, cellular service, road maintenance, privacy and access to outdoor recreation.

Main riskSupply growth
Best-fit operatorRemote capable
04Leisure

Kissimmee, Florida

Study it for: globally recognized family travel and purpose-built vacation-rental communities.

Rule snapshot: Osceola County directs buyers to verify eligible zoning, obtain the Florida vacation-rental license and register for the local business tax receipt.

Main riskExact zoning
Best-fit operatorHigh-turnover
Verify with Osceola County ↗
05Urban

Columbus, Ohio

Study it for: a blend of university, healthcare, corporate, family and event stays.

Micro-location: hospital and campus access, parking, noise patterns and block-by-block guest appeal.

Main riskRule changes
Best-fit operatorUrban systems
06Leisure

Asheville, North Carolina

Study it for: food, culture, mountain access and a recognizable destination brand.

Micro-location: city versus county jurisdiction, drive time, views, road conditions and property type.

Main riskJurisdiction
Best-fit operatorDetail-oriented

How to use this list

A shortlist starts the work. It doesn’t finish it.

A

Pick two archetypes

Compare one drive-to leisure market with one diversified urban or resort market.

B

Call the rule-makers

Speak with planning, licensing and tax offices using a real address or parcel.

C

Walk the competitive set

Study what the best-reviewed listings promise—and where the mediocre ones create friction.
